    Corollary 12.1: the radical grading of ind(mod B) is C #

    deformation-refinements.tex: "The Hom normalization makes the M_i^B indecomposable and pairwise nonisomorphic. Proposition 6.5(3) identifies their categorical radical grading with C."

    Formalization. The hypotheses of Proposition 6.5(3) hold for the evaluated modules of A₀ (liftHyp, and the graded Hom category is generated in degree one, hgen), so the qth power of the categorical radical of the lifted modules is the filtration order ≥ q (mem_radPow_lifted). Leading terms identify rad^q / rad^{q+1} with the degree-q part of C (leadL: surjective, kernel rad^{q+1}), compatibly with composition (leadC_comp).

    The hypotheses of Proposition 6.5(3) #

        Corollary 12.1 (cor:positive-deformation-completeness) for mesh data whose positive degrees are radical. Every positive filtered deformation B of A₀ is representation-finite; the lifted modules M_x^B (which exist, Proposition 6.5) are indecomposable, pairwise nonisomorphic and exhaust the indecomposable B-modules; the qth radical power of ind(mod B) is the filtration order ≥ q, and leading terms identify rad^q / rad^{q+1} with C_q, compatibly with composition: gr_J ind(mod B) ≅ C with these labels.

        Corollary 12.1 for the algebra A₀ of a basic representation-finite algebra A (Construction 2.8): every positive filtered deformation B of A₀ is representation-finite, the lifted modules M_x^B are a skeleton of ind(mod B), and gr_J ind(mod B) ≅ k(Γ_A) with these labels.
